title: negotiated-structured-output-with-hinted-strict-mode-and-friendly-error-mapping
author: Maya Thompson
description: Context: customers asked for clearer schema validation behavior when using response_format and for better UX when streaming partially-invalid structured outputs. This PR introduces a negotiated strictness mode with developer hints, a human-friendly error mapping layer, and safer streaming semantics to preserve tool/function-calling integration. Motivation: previously streaming clients would receive raw JSON errors or abrupt disconnects when schema validation failed mid-stream and tool-calls could be interleaved in invalid states. Goals: 1) let callers express a preference (response_format.schema_version + response_format.strict_hint) without breaking compatibility, 2) emit deterministic machine-level error frames and friendlier human-facing diagnostics, 3) ensure tool/function calls remain fenced and either committed or cleanly aborted on schema failure, 4) keep OpenAI-compat adapter behavior backward compatible for v1/chat and completions. What changed (high level): added a response_format.hint header and an enum for strict_hint (prefer_coercion|strict|soft), implemented a negotiation step in the compatibility layer that chooses coercion/retry/fallback strategies, introduced a "schema-error-frame" streaming chunk type with an attached "human_message" string for client UX, and added fences around tool_call lifecycle so partial outputs don't trigger tool execution. API surface: new optional fields in request payload: response_format.schema_version (string), response_format.strict_hint (string), response_format.hint_metadata (string). The OpenAI-compatibility adapter maps these into internal negotiation decisions while preserving existing v1 endpoints when these fields are absent. Streaming semantics: when a schema violation is detected mid-stream the runtime emits a schema-error-frame then either attempts one soft coercion pass (when prefer_coercion is set) or terminates the stream with a final_error_frame. For strict mode the stream halts immediately and the model output is captured as a diagnostic artifact available via the execution id. Tool/function calling: tool calls are now gated behind a committed-output marker; the runtime will not forward a tool_call to the tool process until a checkpoint confirms the preceding structured tokens conform to the schema or until strict_hint allows speculative tool execution. This prevents side effects from partially-invalid outputs. Error mapping: introduced a compact error taxonomy (schema_mismatch, coercion_failure, stream_truncation, tool_call_fenced, adapter_incompatible) and each error includes a short human_message and actionable_hint. Backwards compatibility: default behavior unchanged when response_format fields are omitted. Testing: unit tests for negotiation logic, integration tests for streaming error frames and tool fences, e2e with OpenAI-compat endpoints. Rollout plan: feature-flagged behind ff/structured-negotiation for 2 weeks, default to opt-in via header. Checklist: - [x] design doc linked - [x] unit tests - [x] integration tests - [x] docs updated - [x] feature flag added - [ ] perf soak in staging
